ns0:entry.ns0:title: [OpenAI]Weeks to Hours: SentinelOne on Cybersecurity Research with OpenAI

ns2:group.ns2:title: Weeks to Hours: SentinelOne on Cybersecurity Research with OpenAI
ns2:group.ns2:description:
Cybersecurity research, moving from weeks to hours.
SentinelOne’s Gregor Stewart describes OpenAI’s cyber capabilities reaching human-level output in about eight hours on reverse-engineering work that would take a top researcher four to six weeks.
That lets security teams investigate more malware, connect related threats and keep a clearer picture of how attacks are evolving.
“That’s a kind of intelligence that we were never able to afford before.”
Watch Gregor explain what faster research makes possible.

ns0:entry.ns0:title: [OpenAI]Block on Finding and Fixing Security Risks with OpenAI

ns2:group.ns2:title: Block on Finding and Fixing Security Risks with OpenAI
ns2:group.ns2:description:
“Now you know and now you can take action before someone else knows.”
A weakness in your code can be part of a much bigger attack. Seeing how those weaknesses connect gives defenders a clearer picture of where to act.
Block’s Chief Information Security Officer, James Nettesheim, shares how OpenAI’s cyber capabilities can help uncover software vulnerabilities and connect them into a path to compromise.
Then comes the work that turns discovery into action: identify the affected software and its owner, propose a patch, and verify that the fix works, with a person guiding deployment.
Watch James on what AI can make possible for cybersecurity teams—from vulnerability analysis and hidden security risks to patch verification and the next steps defenders can take.
